description: Chain level joint translation. A confirmed chain is translated as one unit: its members are merged into a single source text, that text is translated whole with at most one semantic request, and the translation is cut back into one piece per member. Everything the two halves of that round trip need is declared here. output_token_budget and output_token_ratio bound how large a chain may be sent as one unit: the engine is called with a fixed output ceiling, and a request whose answer would reach it comes back truncated rather than refused, which no conservation check downstream can undo. The expected answer is estimated as the merged source token count times output_token_ratio -- measured at about 0.9 for a display line and 1.2 for running text on an English to Chinese pair, so the shipped coefficient carries a safety factor -- and a chain whose estimate exceeds output_token_budget remains protected and untranslated. The budget sits below the engine's own ceiling to leave room for the JSON envelope the answer is wrapped in. join says how two consecutive members are put back together, and records the separator it used so the merge can be read back. profiles say what a sentence end looks like in the target language and where a cut may legally land in it; the profile is chosen by the target language tag, longest declared prefix first, falling back to the default. strategies say which redistribution a chain is cut by, read from the endpoint pair class the chain was built under, never from a page type or a publication. A body chain is cut on sentence boundaries and falls back to a proportional cut only for the members no boundary is left for; a display line chain has no sentence structure to cut on and is proportional throughout. Every cut is a position in the translated string and nothing but the one page break hyphen is ever added or removed, so the pieces always join back to exactly the translation that came in. Punctuation is written as JSON unicode escapes to keep this file ASCII. A display line chain is cut by source share and deterministic target-language boundaries. cut_align_switch remains a compatibility switch for existing profiles, but it never authorizes member translation requests; when enabled, the joint target still uses the same deterministic source weights, punctuation snap and later typesetter capacity measurements. Where the joint translation reorders across a boundary there is no model-derived aligned cut to find, so the placement degrades to share plus snap with the damage bounded by cut_snap_radius.

join.description: How consecutive members are merged. A member whose last character is a trailing hyphen is a word the page break cut in half, so the hyphen is dropped and the halves close up; the hyphen is kept when it stands alone as a word, which is what the preceding character being a space tells us. Two members that meet where neither side is written with interword spaces close up as well: spaceless_script_ranges lists the code point ranges, low..high in hexadecimal, whose scripts set no space between words. Everything else takes the default separator. Nothing else is added to or removed from a member.

profiles.description: One sentence model per target script. terminators end a sentence wherever they stand. space_gated_terminators end one only when whitespace or the end of the text follows, which is what keeps a decimal point, a version number and an in-word full stop from ending a sentence; the two lists together must not be empty. closers are the marks stripped after a terminator before the gate is read, so a quoted sentence still ends where the quotation does. A run of terminators is one boundary and the last character of the run decides whether the gate applies. non_terminal_prefixes are the abbreviations that carry a terminator and a space and still do not end a sentence; the table is read before the gate, so a boundary whose text ends in one of them is dropped whatever the gate would have said. A prefix matches only where the character in front of it is not a letter or a digit, so a longer word ending in the same letters is not mistaken for it. sentence_min_chars is the shortest sentence a boundary may close, counted in non-space characters: below it the boundary is dropped and the text carries on into the next sentence, which is what absorbs single letter initials. It is bounded by the range the flat sentence_min_chars declares. break_rule says where a proportional cut may land: word_boundary only after whitespace, any_char anywhere a combining sequence is not broken. language_prefixes match the target language tag, longest first; a prefix may be declared by one profile only.

strategies.description: Which redistribution a chain is cut by, keyed by the endpoint pair class the chain was built under in chain_detection.json. tail_aligned is what a broken running paragraph takes: the cut is put where the source character shares put it, renormalized over the members still unserved, and then pulled back to the last line end the member's own box actually reached, so the member closes on a line it filled and the part line it could not hold moves on whole to the member after it. Whether the tail line is full is answered by measurement and never by a width ratio, so no threshold appears here; a paragraph broken by a column edge and one broken by a page edge are cut the same way. capacity instead fills the first box to the brim, which leaves the member ending mid line whenever the two boxes differ in width, and it is kept as the level below tail_aligned and as what an unmeasurable box falls back to. sentence_greedy assigns whole sentences to members by their share of the source and cuts proportionally only where no sentence boundary is left, which it reports as a proportional fallback. proportional cuts by share throughout and claims no sentence structure. A pair class not named here takes the default. slot_cascade is the order a chain with measurable source boxes tries the strategies in, first success winning: a tail aligned split that hands a later member more text than its own box holds is an ordinary outcome and falls to the level below, not an error. Every name in it must be implemented.

tail_align.description: The bounds on the tail aligned cut. The judgement itself carries no threshold: whether a share estimate already stands at a line end is answered by measuring the member's own box, not by comparing a filled width against a ratio. These two numbers bound only what that measurement may cost and how little of a member it may leave. max_probes caps how many times one interior cut may re-measure its box while binary searching for the last line end at or before the estimate, so a box of up to two to the max_probes lines is searched completely and a taller one settles for an earlier line end rather than costing more. min_kept_lines is how many lines the member must still hold after the pull back; below it the estimate stands where it was and the sidecar says so, because a member pulled back past its first line would be left with nothing to show.

capacity.description: Legacy deterministic grid retained for pure redistribution compatibility checks. The live continuity-chain path measures target text with the typesetter's mapped fonts and line packer and does not consume these character estimates.

line_head_forbidden_punctuation_descript: The marks a target fragment may not open with. The list is pinned to the typesetter's line-head punctuation class.
line_tail_forbidden_punctuation_descript: The opening marks a target fragment may not end with. The list is pinned to the typesetter's line-tail punctuation class.
